abstract: Current computational methods for analyzing viruses in human metagenomes rely on static databases composed largely of fragmented virus genomes, which are mostly derived from gastrointestinal samples. This issue limits the identification of viruses exclusively found outside the gastrointestinal tract and impairs analyses requiring high-quality genomes. To address these issues, we created the Updateable Human Virome Database (UHVDB), an expandable database of 1.15 million high-quality, clustered, and annotated virus genomes integrated from pre-existing human virome databases and diverse human sample metagenome assemblies. We developed an associated toolkit that enables users to (i) update UHVDB by mining, clustering, and annotating virus sequences, (ii) taxonomically profile viruses in metagenomes and metatranscriptomes, (iii) estimate phage replication activity using phage-to-host ratios, and (iv) determine the genomic characteristics of detected viruses. To illustrate the utility of UHVDB and its associated toolkit, we analyzed 1949 oral/airway samples from people with cystic fibrosis and a separate dataset of metatranscriptomes from people with acute respiratory infections. UHVDB is a novel framework for virome analysis that expands the capacity to define virus contributions to health and disease.
